result.note: Tests the UK's recognition of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under UK CBAM: start date and sectors covered.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the United Kingdom's decision in September 2026 relating to India and the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM):
items: The UK recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under its incoming border carbon tax.
The UK CBAM is scheduled to begin on 1 January 2027.
The decision spares Indian exporters of iron, steel, aluminium and cement from double taxation.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. Britain recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, so exporters of iron, steel, aluminium and cement avoid double taxation when UK CBAM starts on 1 January 2027. The move cleared one of the two measures that had stalled the India-UK trade pact.
questions.source: sparing exporters of iron, steel, aluminium, and cement from double taxation when UK CBAM begins on January 1, 2027
